author: JILL ZIMA BORSKI
title: School board sets preliminary budget - NewsBreak
text:
By JILL ZIMA BORSKI ,
5 hours ago
PLANTATION KEY — During a Monroe County School District budget workshop Aug. 19 at Coral Shores High School, officials indicated that the average homeowner can expect to pay about $82 more in property taxes to the district for the 2025-2026 budget compared to the current year.
Tax notices were to be mailed Aug. 24 and the school district is to have a final budget hearing Sept. 9 at Marathon High School.
Appraisals for homesteaded residential property can increase up to 2.9% per year (plus any improvements) due to a cap set by the Save Our Homes Amendment. The overall assessed property values in Monroe County, which include commercial and non-homesteaded residential property, increased by 4.71%.
Approving the resolution to adopt the tentative budget for 2025-2026, school board member Sue Woltanski of Tavernier said the average appraised value of a home in Monroe County is $500,000 and would experience an increase of $82.16 in taxes this year for a total of $1,442.56 due to a total millage of 2.9470. Ninety percent of the schools’ budget comes from property values; 10% comes from the state.
The district expects a $12 million increase in construction costs and is designating $9.5 million for a hurricane fund. The school district annually pays the county sheriff’s office $1.866 million to have school resource officers in the schools.
Executive Director of Operations and Planning Patrick Lefere shared construction updates on the Islamorada Founders Park baseball field improvements and Rex Weech field improvements in Key West — both of which are to include a press box and restrooms — and the Reynolds School renovation in Key West. The next step for Founders Park will be drafting share use and licensing agreements between Islamorada and school district. The district also approved an interim agreement extension/ground lease with TVC Development Inc. for the Trumbo affordable workforce housing project in Key West.
Board member Mindy Conn seeks a construction expert to look over the athletic fields documents and prices to advise the school board.
“We don’t have an expert on fields. It would help me to spend money if we knew (more),” she said.
